newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany, Russia up cooperation with new credit deal.
newsitem.headline: Germany, Russia up cooperation with new credit deal.

text.p: German-Russian cooperation intensified on Monday when Deutsche Bank AG said it had been mandated by Vneshekonombank to arrange a one billion mark ($585 million) credit package to finance German goods exports to Russia.

In a further fillip for economic cooperation between the two countries, the bank said Russia would issue its mark-denominated Eurobond as planned and that the exact timing had not been decided yet. There had been reports that the issue would be delayed.
"Helping the Russian economy to stabilise and start to grow requires foreign investment," Russian Economics Minister Yevgeny Yasin told a German-Russian investment conference.

Deutsche management board member Georg Krupp said trade between Germany and Russia was worth 19 billion marks in the first nine months of 1996, less than Germany trades with Poland, and had strong potential for growth.
The speed at which the Russian economy was being opened up was but risks still remained, he said.
"Despite the obvious positive development in Russia, trading partners and banks have had to deal with problems and the risks are still high," said Krupp.
Deutsche said that the billion mark agreement between it and Vneshekonombank had come about following talks with the Russian Finance Ministry.

The package had two components -- a tranche backed by the German state-backed Hermes export credit guarantee scheme to cover 85 percent of the investment good deliveries and a further tranche, which will not be covered by Hermes, to cover the remaining 15 percent.

Deutsche and Vneshekonombank said in a statement they were considering involving AKA Ausfuhrkredit-Gesellschaft mbH, the German Export Credit Company, an organisation experienced in Russian credit business.
Deutsche plans to invite AKA's consortium banks to contribute towards the financing package.
The aim of the agreement is to create the conditions for a rapid use of this year's Hermes credit guarantees in the interest of German exporters and Russian importers.
The Russian Finance Ministry had on Friday denied reports that the mark-denominated Eurobond could be delayed.
"Russia will issue the bond on the German market as planned but there is no final decision on the timing yet," a Deutsche Bank spokesman told Reuters in confirmation on Monday.
He added that Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits would attend a presentation on the bond for investors in Frankfurt on March 12.
The bond, for up to two billion marks, is expected to have a maturity of seven years.

The Finance Ministry denial came after a syndicate manager at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, joint lead manager of the deal, said Russia might not launch its Eurobond this week as expected if sentiment in the emerging market sector of the bond market did not improve.

Russian officials have said the bond may be issued on March 13 after the roadshow for investors. There will be a presentation for investors in Zurich on March 11. --Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.707 German Marks)
